subject: Biotechnology
title: Activated Sludge Process
description: A micro-lesson that makes Activated Sludge Process usable.

hook.text: Every flush sends waste to a treatment plant — billions of bacteria in activated sludge clean water before it returns to rivers.

buildup.text: Aeration tanks bubble air through wastewater — aerobic bacteria consume organic matter, converting it to CO2 and biomass.

discovery.text: Settled sludge is recycled back to the aeration tank — maintaining a dense bacterial community that cleans incoming sewage.

twist.text: Activated sludge uses 1 to 2% of a country's total electricity — aeration is energy-intensive and contributes to carbon emissions.

climax.text: Anammox bacteria remove nitrogen without aeration — saving 60% of energy costs in wastewater nutrient removal.

punchline.text: Bacteria clean our water — activated sludge is the world's largest biotechnology.

quiz.question: How do anammox bacteria improve wastewater treatment?
options: They remove phosphorus without any chemical addition
They remove nitrogen without requiring energy-intensive aeration, saving up to 60% of energy costs
They convert sludge directly into drinking water
